correctness.rationale: The two-sublattice adjacency map is exactly the block operator with Laurent symbols 1+X+Y and 1+X^{-1}+Y^{-1}. Frobenius splitting over F4 yields seven invertible frequency factors and two bad ones. At each bad factor the nonzero Jacobian establishes independent parameters p and q in F4[p,q]/(p^k,q^k). Explicit ranks of powers of [[0,p],[q,0]] are 2(k-t)^2 at even stages and 2(k-t-1)(k-t) at odd stages; two bad factors yield the stated ranks and four blocks of each odd Jordan size. Fitting decomposition gives every exponent in the transient census and last-step fraction. C++17 checker independently verified ranks through 2k for k=1,2,4,8 and exhausted all 262144 labelled k=1 states; computations corroborate rather than substitute for the uniform proof.

originality.rationale: Primary-source comparison covered the two-sublattice honeycomb tight-binding symbol and its two complex zero modes, general finite-group additive automata, and hexagonal cellular-automaton rule-matrix studies. The new claim is an explicit characteristic-two Jordan decomposition and complete sharp transient census for every toroidal size 3 times a power of two. Neither the inspected results nor searched published records state or imply that filtration. The 1993 toroidal-polyhex source could not be inspected beyond its abstract, and unindexed duplication remains possible.

value.rationale: The chosen family is forced naturally by the two order-three singular honeycomb Fourier points and the characteristic-two Frobenius thickening. An explicit odd-Jordan ladder for a two-sublattice graph, an unbounded sharp maximum transient 2k-1, an exact all-depth state count and a k-independent 15/16 maximal-depth fraction are structural invariants of a natural connected cubic torus family, not an arbitrary finite parameter slice or routine table entry.
